niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Decision Fatigue: Why You Buy Junk at Night
ideas.angle: The video reveals how the brain's willpower is a finite resource, explaining why we make poor decisions like impulse buying or snacking late in the day when our 'mental energy' is depleted.

hook.en: Your brain has a daily battery.
hook.fr: Ton cerveau a une batterie quotidienne.

ideas.reason: Search trends for productivity and 'burnout' are high. This explains a universal frustration (poor evening choices) with a scientific mechanism, leading to high shareability.
sources: Baumeister, R. F. (2002). Yielding to Temptation: Self-Regulatory Failure, Impulsive Purchasing, and Consumer Behavior. Journal of Consumer Research.

ideas.title: Why Your Brain Hates Good News
ideas.angle: It explains the Negativity Bias: our brains are evolved to prioritize one bad event over ten good ones for survival, which is why we obsess over a single criticism.

hook.en: One insult ruins your whole day.
hook.fr: Une insulte gâche toute ta journée.

ideas.reason: Social media comments and 'hate-watching' are current cultural peaks. Explaining why we focus on the negative provides instant relief and validation to the viewer.
sources: Baumeister, R. F., et al. (2001). Bad Is Stronger Than Good. Review of General Psychology.

ideas.title: Get People to Like You by Asking for a Favor
ideas.angle: Counter-intuitively, asking someone for a small favor makes them like you more because their brain justifies the effort by assuming you are worth helping.

hook.en: Want a friend? Ask for help.
hook.fr: Tu veux un ami ? Demande de l'aide.

ideas.reason: Social 'hacks' and networking tips are evergreen. This specific paradox is highly engaging because it contradicts the common fear that asking for help bothers people.
sources: Jecker, J., & Landy, D. (1969). Liking a Person as a Function of Doing Him a Favor. Human Relations.
